findings.claim: Ledger L8 says metadata-only types are deliberately not analysed, with no MsgPack diagnostics for them. The change drops diagnostics for metadata-located types, which matches that convention, so the missing diagnostic is deliberate and not a defect.

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed; the defining assembly owns validating its own types. A dropped MsgPack004 for a metadata generic struct is not a defect.

findings.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter wraps every reportDiagnostic call, so it can silently suppress diagnostics beyond the metadata case, such as diagnostics located in other compilations or in generated trees. The change does not show tests that existing diagnostics MsgPack003/004/005 still fire for same-assembly types after the wrapper. L10 says these diagnostics have had false-positive churn.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer test suite (MsgPack003/004/005 and similar) and confirm it still passes. Add a test that a MemberNeedsKey diagnostic on a same-compilation closed generic struct is still reported.

findings.claim: The new README section and the MsgPack004 doc describe behaviour recorded in L8. README section placement and wording are fine, but the README says that diagnostics are reported by the defining assembly. This holds only if that assembly is built with the analyzer, which is not guaranteed for NuGet packages, so the claim is slightly overbroad.

receipt_plan.detail: README.md new section 'Generic types from referenced assemblies' asserts that the defining assembly reports problems. L8 records this as deliberate, but the rationale is only inferred.
